subject: Pilot top-up vouchers and milestone-based extensions
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@brightwave.ai>

Cc: BrightWave Procurement <procurement@brightwave.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick ask — pilot top-up vs time extension

Hi Olga,

Hope you're well. We're at about 78% of the pilot credits after two weeks of heavy usage (see attached usage_report_q4.csv) and have two internal asks: one from product (they want another 2 weeks to finish a secondary evaluation) and one from procurement (they'd prefer to avoid re-contracting for a longer term).

Question: Would Redwood consider a credit top-up (one-time voucher) that we can apply against the current pilot instead of a straight time extension? If so, what structure do you recommend — a %-based top-up, a fixed-credit voucher, or milestone-locked credits (e.g., additional credits that unlock after a demo/hand-off)?

We also need a short note for procurement listing any changes to pricing/discounts so they can issue a PO quickly.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Product
BrightWave Analytics

Attachment: usage_report_q4.csv (CSV, 92KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick ask — pilot top-up vs time extension

Hi Samira — thanks for the context and the usage file. Short answer: yes, we can do a voucher/top-up instead of extending calendar time. Two pragmatic options that work for most POC flows:

- Option A — Fixed credit top-up: a one-time credit (e.g., 25% of current consumption) usable immediately against the pilot. Simple for procurement and bookkeeping; credits expire 90 days after issuance.
- Option B — Milestone voucher: credits are issued in two tranches. Tranche 1 (50%) issued immediately; Tranche 2 (50%) released after a milestone (demo, integration checkpoint). This aligns incentives for product and gives procurement a conditional spend pattern.

If procurement prefers not to touch discounts, we can keep list pricing and issue a promotional credit (voucher) instead of a formal discount line on the PO. That usually preserves renewal MTAs.

I'll loop Ben on the operational numbers and Marissa for success/hand-off. Ben — can you draft two concrete structures (credit amounts + expiry) and a one-line procurement note? Marissa — any objections on the milestone definition?

Cheers,
Olga
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 11:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick ask — pilot top-up vs time extension

Samira / team — attached is a short proposal (proposal_brightwave_v1.pdf) with two alternatives laid out and exact credit math based on your reported consumption. Highlights:

- Alternative 1 (Fixed top-up): +30% credit top-up (one-time), credits valid for 90 days, no change to PO line item (we'll issue a voucher code). Estimated additional tokens: ~2.3M, value listed at $8,900 at pilot rates.
- Alternative 2 (Milestone voucher): 50% issued now, 50% on post-demo acceptance (demo defined as walkthrough + sign-off by product). Credits valid 120 days for this option. Estimated value $9,600 (we can round for procurement).

Procurement note (single line to include in PO): "One-time promotional voucher issued by Redwood Inference applied to pilot consumption; no change to published pilot rate card. Voucher redeemable per attached terms."

If you want a short SLA amendment (2-week window vs. 30-day invoice terms) we can include it as an addendum — otherwise voucher issuance and code is the fastest.

Ben Carter
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposal_brightwave_v1.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

- Please confirm the voucher expiry in writing (you note 120 days) and whether partial redemption is allowed.
- We need a one-line commercial note for the PO referencing the voucher code.
- Can you shorten the SLA addendum language so legal can sign off fast (1–2 business days review)?

Once we have those, procurement will issue a PO the same day. Marissa — can your CS team confirm the milestone acceptance criteria (demo + integration checklist)?

On our side procurement will route a $9,600 PO to Redwood.

Samira
